items.title: Leonid Activity: Bright Fireballs Have a Natural Baseline
items.what_changed: The Leonids peaked around November 17–18. The meteoroid network report reproduced by Spaceweather.com lists 76 November 18 fireballs, including 35 Leonids and seven Northern Taurids.
items.status: Ordinary meteoroid observations, not verified anomalous craft. The count refers to network detections on a specific date.
items.why_watch: Maintain natural-sky baselines before classifying any unusual video or witness report.

items.title: Black Triangle: Federal Witness Statements Make This a Priority Case
items.source: CBS News · PURSUE FBI statement and AARO debrief
items.what_changed: The October 23 PURSUE release included a signed FBI witness statement and an AARO debrief about a June 2026 observation near an unspecified western-US national-security site. Two agents described a small matte-black triangular object observed after a third agent alerted them; the records describe a silent vertical ascent, brief hover and rapid departure. This is a closer review of an existing release, not a new November 19 incident.
items.status: Government release and existence of witness accounts confirmed. Reported motion and thermal properties are testimony, not independently validated flight-performance measurements; no public identification or extraterrestrial conclusion established. AARO said the similarities to other accounts warrant further investigation.
items.why_watch: Obtain original memo and signed statements, distinguish firsthand recollections from interpretations, seek original sensor footage and geometry, and compare independent corroboration before escalating the conclusion.

items.title: Alaska Jellyfish Video: Kite or Balloon Remains Plausible
items.what_changed: A video recorded by Sara Jane Osborn near Anchorage on June 15 around 10:13 p.m. circulated widely in November. Former AARO director Sean Kirkpatrick said the motion resembles a streamer kite; other analysts discussed a kite or high-altitude balloon. Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson reported no further information.
items.status: Reported video and named eyewitness are documented; image authenticity opinions are not independent verification of the object or its distance and scale. Kite and balloon remain hypotheses, not confirmed identifications.
items.why_watch: Prioritize original continuous video, wind and weather, apparent motion, flight logs and optical geometry. Avoid presenting proximity to the base as evidence of military involvement.

items.title: Oregon Family Describes Lights and Later Symptoms; Cause Unknown
items.category: UAP / WITNESS CLAIM / HEALTH CAUSATION UNVERIFIED
items.what_changed: A November media report revisited an August 25 Wilsonville, Oregon family account. NUFORC logged the report and an August 29 investigator interview describing a silver/translucent-looking object and lights near a bedroom, with later self-reported nausea, balance complaints and headaches.
items.status: The witness report and interview are documented, but the object's identity, size and distance are unverified. No independent medical evaluation establishes symptoms or a causal link to the reported sighting. NUFORC said police received no other UAP reports that evening.
items.why_watch: Seek original image metadata, independent local observations, flight and drone activity, and medical documentation only with the family's consent; do not imply a radiation or poisoning hazard.

items.title: Forty Years Since JAL Flight 1628's Alaska Encounter
items.what_changed: On November 17, 1986, a Japan Air Lines cargo crew reported unusual lights and objects over Alaska. The FAA later released its investigation records and said it could not confirm the reported UFO event.
items.status: Historically documented crew report; disputed radar interpretations and testimony do not establish the objects' identity. Yesterday marked the fortieth anniversary.
items.why_watch: Revisit original flight logs, witness interviews, independent radar interpretations and the FAA's own qualification rather than retell embellished versions.

items.title: The Doomsday Date That Came and Went
items.what_changed: A genuine 1960 Science paper by von Foerster, Mora and Amiot extrapolated historical population growth toward a mathematical singularity on Friday, November 13, 2026.
items.status: Published mathematical extrapolation, not a validated apocalypse forecast. The date passed without the predicted infinite population.
items.why_watch: Ask what assumptions make an elegant curve fail when extrapolated beyond the data; revisit original text before repeating apocalypse headlines.

items.title: Northern Taurids Peak Tonight: A Natural Fireball Reference
items.body: The Northern Taurids peak November 11–12 under very favorable moonlight conditions. The shower has modest meteor rates but can produce bright fireballs. Record exact location, time, viewing direction and imagery before labeling a moving light anomalous. This is a normal astronomical event, not evidence of UAP.
items.status: Confirmed

items.title: NASA's November Skywatching Guide Adds a Useful Baseline
items.body: NASA projects the Northern Taurids around November 12, a Mars–Jupiter pairing on November 15–16, and Leonid activity November 17–18. These predictable events belong beside extraordinary sky reports so that a bright point, fireball or close planetary pairing is not mistaken for unexplained technology.
items.status: Confirmed

items.title: UAP Disclosure Advocates Keep Their Seats
items.body: Cybernews reports that Anna Paulina Luna, Tim Burchett, Eric Burlison, and Jared Moskowitz won reelection, preserving several visible bipartisan advocates for UAP disclosure in Congress. The election keeps those lawmakers in place; it does not verify UAP claims or guarantee new hearings or document releases.

items.title: Evidence Check: The “Cold Orbs” Clips Are Screen Recordings
items.body: In its August 7 release, AARO says the referenced clips were recorded from a phone filming an infrared sensor display, rather than supplied as native sensor data. It warns that this limits image fidelity and says its descriptions should not be read as an analytical conclusion about what the objects were. Preserve the case as unresolved; record the sensor chain and limits.

items.title: $100,000 Award Funds a Consciousness–UAP Research Proposal
items.body: The Institute of Noetic Sciences announced its 2026 research-prize winner on November 5: a multidisciplinary team proposing research on consciousness-associated UAP experiences. The award funds investigation; it does not establish extraterrestrial origins, paranormal mechanisms, or a validated connection.

items.title: Northern Taurids: Keep Natural Fireballs in the Reference Set
items.body: NASA's November skywatching guidance places the Northern Taurid peak around November 12. Occasional bright fireballs are expected within a generally low-rate meteor shower. Record time, location and trajectory when evaluating unusual lights; do not label an unidentified sighting exotic by default.

items.title: NASA Revisits a Major Taurid Fireball
items.body: NASA's November 8 Astronomy Picture of the Day features a 2017 fireball over the Dolomites, with reported observations consistent with the Northern Taurid meteor stream. The image is new to today's feature; the meteor itself is historical, not a fresh 2026 event.
items.source: NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day · Nov 8, 2026

items.title: Northern Taurids Near Their November Peak
items.body: NASA expects the Northern Taurids to peak around November 12. Rates are generally low—around five meteors per hour under ideal conditions—but occasional fireballs can be spectacular. A bright meteor is not, by itself, evidence of unusual technology.

items.title: A Gamma-Ray Burst Gets a Fresh Alert
items.body: The SVOM mission team reported triggering on gamma-ray burst GRB 261108A at 01:13:20 UTC on November 8, with a low-latency location estimate. This is an instrument alert from a scientific team, not a claim about danger to Earth or exotic visitors.

items.title: Black Triangle File: Observation Is Not Identification
items.body: An independent UAP weekly digest discusses disagreement over a reported black-triangle account in newly released files. Witness testimony merits preservation, but without complete sensor data and chain of evidence the object's identity remains unresolved. We should track the original record and skeptical evaluations together.
